summary: FireFusion is an advanced real-time web service designed to harmonize and analyze active-fire detections from multiple satellite datasets, specifically integrating MODIS and VIIRS observations. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge by team Cosmic Conquistadors, FireFusion provides an intuitive interactive dashboard and an analyst review queue that transforms complex satellite data into actionable intelligence. By bridging the gap between raw Earth observation data and rapid wildfire monitoring, FireFusion empowers emergency responders and analysts to detect, track, and assess wildfire threats faster and more efficiently, ultimately protecting ecosystems and communities.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? FireFusion is an advanced, analyst-focused wildfire intelligence platform designed to detect, track, and analyze active wildfire threats. It works by ingesting and harmonizing real satellite telemetry data from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors. The platform processes thermal anomalies to generate global satellite heatmaps, calculates cross-sensor co-occurrence via the Fire Agreement Index (FAI), and surfaces candidate locations into structured analyst review queues.

What benefits does it have?

  • Unified Intelligence: Combines MODIS (MCD14DL) and NOAA-20/21 VIIRS observations into a single, transparent review workflow.
  • Cross-Sensor Validation: Uses the Fire Agreement Index (FAI) to help analysts identify locations where multiple satellite systems report fire activity within the same space-time context.
  • Comprehensive Dashboards: Offers intuitive user interfaces combining global fire activity maps, burning activity calendars, and detailed candidate verification panels.

What is the intended impact of the project? The intended impact of FireFusion is to drastically improve disaster response efficiency for emergency management teams and environmental monitoring authorities. By transforming fragmented satellite observations into structured candidate groups, the platform helps analysts prioritize threats faster, streamline triage time, and protect vulnerable communities and ecosystems.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, TailwindCSS, Leaflet, and Recharts.
  • Backend & Data Processing: FastAPI, Python, Pandas, and GeoPandas.
  • Deployment Architecture: Docker-based containerization bundling the frontend, backend, and NASA FIRMS datasets into a single optimized deployment unit.

How is your project creative? FireFusion creatively bridges the gap between raw scientific satellite telemetry and practical operational tools. Rather than treating all fire detections as equal or overwhelming operators with isolated data feeds, it introduces a transparent harmonization layer and cross-sensor co-occurrence proxy (FAI) that respects source provenance while simplifying multi-system analysis.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific Transparency: Ensuring the platform preserves native confidence systems and source provenance completely while clearly outlining its boundaries (e.g., serving as an analyst support tool rather than an automated life-safety system).
  • User Workflow & Usability: Designing structured triage queues and interactive maps that allow analysts to inspect source-level information efficiently under high-pressure scenarios.
  • Data Scale & Integration: Effectively harmonizing hundreds of thousands of real NASA FIRMS records into a cohesive, performant application architecture.
